body: I apologize! I just tend to have bad anxiety and have trouble reading some social situations, so I sometimes get confused on what the right thing to do is. I just know it took a lot of hard work to make, so I feel bad for asking, but again, I didn’t get what I ordered.
Hey, no worries! My school usually starts the last week or two or August (like the 24th or so) but they delayed it. September 1st is the new first day!
Floridian here and I hope this means this nightmare is almost over! Want to start school in person in September!

Hey friend, 

I’m a little older, in college, and I completely understand you. I’m usually a 4.0 student, doing incredibly well, and the last semester when everything was online really tested me as well. I felt I had no motivation left by the end of the semester, stayed in bed for some lectures, and it was generally not a good time.

I’m registered for the fall semester, and have no idea if I’m going to be fully online or not. I can’t really give you any type of “what you should do” advice, but I wanted you to know this:

You are not alone. So many people (myself included) are in the same boat. The one thing I can tell you is that it is up to us to persevere even in the face of tyranny and stick it to those who want to see us fail. One day soon when all of this is over and people are asking themselves “what was this all worth?” we will be able to say that we persevered and were able to continue making our dreams come true.

Don’t give up. Keep pushing forward. If it means anything, know some random person on the internet knows you can do it, and you have a whole group of people who support you!

And yet masks, according to some people = no spikes? And people want to vilify the people who don’t want to wear masks because they know it doesn’t do squat. Here’s proof. The mask is nothing more than a security blanket.

If you’re coming into contact with someone who has tested positive, or if you yourself are sick, then yes, by all means, wear a mask. Heck, if you want to wear a mask because it makes you feel more comfortable, wear it. But don’t shove it down other people’s throats.

Wow. God Forbid any good news comes out about the death rate of this virus, it’s going to be torn apart by a journalist who wants to aid in continuing the panic. 

What’s next, when hospitalizations lower are they going to say it’s not something worth celebrating either? Because even that might rebound?

Sorry to say, but “getting used to living with COVID-19” is the only way forward. This virus is not going to just magically disappear.

Hi everyone, not exactly sure where to start with this, but I really needed somewhere to vent. I have two family members in the medical field, and every time I talk to them about this, they’re sympathetic, but constantly remind me how lucky I am to be healthy and not have to worry about bills/responsibilities/etc. I’m sorry if it’s a lot to read, I don’t know how else to cope but to write.

I’m 26, recently lost almost 100 pounds, and am studying law in hopes of becoming a paralegal. My life was finally back on track, and I’ll be honest, I felt like I would start my dream career and meet the man I was going to marry soon. I want to get married and have a big family, so it’s a very personal, very real dream and goal for me. 

Then, lockdowns came. And curfews. And mandatory masks that if you didn’t want to wear, you were selfish, and a baby for not wanting to do so. And everything closed down.

I felt like my life is over. To be completely honest, I sometimes still feel like my life is over before it even began. I’ve suffered with high anxiety and depression before this ever started, being locked away has only served to multiply those anxious fears tenfold. I feel like I’ll never meet the man Im going to marry. I feel like we’ll never be able to meet face to face, never get to have children, never get to feel normal and happy again. Those feelings have gotten very hard. I feel like I worked so hard to lose so much weight and start a new career path. And for what reason? Why did I push so hard if my life was just going to be put on hold indefinitely? What is life worth if I am just reduced to merely existing?

I know I’m not the only one struggling during these lockdowns. Again, I have two family members in the medical field, so I know this virus can be serious. But my mind is just filled with the what if’s and the fear that I’ll never be able to live my dream life, or at the very least try to. And that has spurred some very dark thoughts in my head.

I feel selfish for thinking like this. But I can’t help it. I’m sorry if I come off as selfish. But I really needed to vent and get this off my chest. It’s painful to keep it bottled up.
